thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach on /v1/generate in prod (p99 = 2.8s > SLO 0.8s). Triggered by canary-monitor.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: model=rw-model-v4.3, traffic=5% -> 20:05 UTC (canary-id=canary-2026-06-15-01).

Anna (oncall): seeing pager. I'm on it. First check: is this widespread or only canary?

Mike (SRE): dashboard shows spike correlated with canary nodes in us-west-2. p95 also up from 120ms -> 650ms. Streaming stalls visible: several streams stuck at "awaiting tokens".

Ravi (ML Eng): v4.3 introduced a new attention kernel path optimized for 4k context; fallback to generic kernel on some GPUs causes long-tail. Possible kernel selection bug + KV cache invalidation on cold starts.

Emma (CS): we have a customer (Acme Corp) reporting increased timeouts on embeddings/generation callouts — their traffic bucket partially routed to canary. They've flagged a business impact.

Jess (PM): assign priority: customer impact + SLO breach -> P0. What's our mitigation plan? Rollback to v4.2 or reduce canary traffic?

Anna (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) Pause canary traffic, 2) Apply routing fallback to v4.2 for streaming endpoints, 3) Throttle new sessions to canary. Which is fastest?

Ravi (ML Eng): fastest is pause canary traffic. We can flip routing flag to 0% in the router. That avoids risky partial fallbacks. If we need to keep canary, we can route non-streaming calls only.

Mike (SRE): I'm preparing rollback play. Flipping traffic now should be quick. Running command: 
```
# route control
redwood route update --service=generate --canary=canary-2026-06-15-01 --traffic=0
```

deploy-bot: Command executed by Mike: route update accepted. Canary traffic set to 0% at 20:10 UTC.

Anna (oncall): Observability: p99 started trending down 2 minutes after traffic cut. Current p99 = 0.78s. p95 = 130ms. Streaming stalls clearing.

Emma (CS): telling Acme support that we rolled back canary routing and are monitoring. They want ETA on full rollback confirmation and root cause.

Ravi (ML Eng): will capture a heap of kernel selection logs from canary nodes for postmortem. Suspect path: kernel_selector.choose_for_layer(...) returning fallback kernel on ~10% of layers for some model shapes -> tail blowup.

Mike (SRE): initiating postmortem logging snapshot and saving traces: 
```
# grab traces
redwood observability export --filter 'canary-2026-06-15-01' --since 20:00 --until 20:15 -o /tmp/canary-traces-1865436789.tar.gz
```

Anna (oncall): Handoff note for next oncall in 30m: incident mitigated by stopping canary traffic. No further paging expected. Please followup on kernel-selector logs and consider automated canary rollback when p99 > 2x SLO for >5m.

Jess (PM): customer comms: Emma to draft message to Acme with timeline + compensation offer if needed. Also we'll delay v4.3 rollout until ML eng signoff.

Emma (CS): drafting now. Key points: root cause under investigation, immediate mitigation rolled out (canary halted), monitoring shows recovery, we'll provide RCA within 72h.

Ravi (ML Eng): action items: 1) reproduce locally with same GPU kernel stack, 2) add more aggressive canary health checks (p99/p95 + streaming stall detector), 3) add kernel selector telemetry for layer-level fallback rates.

Mike (SRE): ops action items: 1) add automated traffic cut if canary correlated p99 spike > 2x SLO for 3 minutes, 2) run canary smoke tests that simulate long streaming contexts.

Anna (oncall): closing incident channel for now. If anyone sees reoccurrence, @Anna (oncall) or page SRE. Good job everyone for fast rollback. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: canary-induced p99 spike mitigated by routing rollback. Duration: ~10m. Postmortem required.

Emma (CS): note: Acme acknowledged mitigation, appreciated quick reaction. Might escalate if RCA delayed.

Ravi (ML Eng): I'll start triage doc and link traces to the postmortem. Will propose a canary gating checklist.

Jess (PM): we'll schedule a postmortem sync in 48h. Thanks all.
